LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.1 Pythagorean Relationship (4 lessons) By the end of the sub stra
Topic 3.2: Length
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Length, part of Measurements 3.1 Pythagorean Relationship (4 lessons) By the end of the sub stra in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use different units of measuring length? 2. How do we measure the perimeter of different objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Generate conversion tables involving cm, dm, m, Dm, Hm. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or be assisted by their peers to carry out the activity.

2. Carry out different operations involving length.

3. Watch videos on correct procedures of measuring length and working out perimeter. Learners with postural defects could be preferentially positioned during this learning experience. Adjust the light intensity for learners with visual difficulties.

4. Use appropriate measuring tools to measure the length of various objects.

5. Measure and work out in 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Generate conversion tables involving cm, dm, m, Dm, Hm. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or be assisted by their peers to carry out the activity.
2. Carry out different operations involving length.
3. Watch videos on correct procedures of measuring length and working out perimeter. Learners with postural defects could be preferentially positioned during this learning experience. Adjust the light intensity for learners with visual difficulties.
4. Use appropriate measuring tools to measure the length of various objects.
5. Measure and work out in 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Length together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: as the learner works with peers when measuring lengths of various objects and also as

they discuss the relationship between circumference and diameter.

● Self-efficacy: as the learner practices different operations using length.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner relates circumference to diameter.

Values

● Integrity: as the learner carries out the activities and give the correct measurement.

● Unity: as the learner works together in measuring lengths of various objects.
